newsitem.title: USA: Senate Leader Lott says "too late" for CPI budget fix.
newsitem.headline: Senate Leader Lott says "too late" for CPI budget fix.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday it was "too late" for a consumer price index correction to be included in a budget being negotiated with the White House.

Lott made his comment just one day after President Clinton signalled flexibility on the issue of the CPI, which is widely believed to overstate inflation. Federal benefit increases for Social Security and other programmes are tied to the CPI.

Lott, a Mississippi Republican, had pushed for some action on the CPI earlier this year, but was initially rebuffed. Clinton Sunday showed some flexibility saying he was willing to "take some heat" on a cost of living adjustment.

The CPI is a politically-sensitive issue because reducing the cost of living increase would mean a smaller increase in federal benefits tied to it. But it would also mean savings in federal spending and make reducing the budget deficit easier.

"The CPI ... I think that's by the boards now, it's too late," Lott told reporters. "People have hardened, we should have done it in a non-political commission-type atmosphere, we didn't do that," Lott said.

Instead the issues had become politicized and House Republicans and Democrats had made it clear they would not back it. "It's going to be very hard to ask our people in the Senate to walk the plank" on an issue that would spark opposition from elderly and labour groups, Lott said.
Lott said President Clinton needed to "sober up" and cut back on the domestic spending increases that he was seeking. He planned to speak with Clinton on Tuesday.

The Senate leader said he was seeking from the president "a recognition that the spending increases he wants are just not practical, some dramatic move away from that," Lott said. He said the White House was talking about $120 billion to $130 billion in new spending over five years for domestic programs.
"There's still hope that something dramatic will happen here in the next couple, three days," Lott said. "We've waited as long as we can, this is the week," he added.
